A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOAM study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E are readable and can be matched despite pagination and proof revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original C4 pre-training experiments, GLUE and MMLU fine-tuning results, and optimizer ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds LDAdamW results to the LLaMA pre-training comparison.

M1.justification: The block averaging, fold/unfold operators, residual corrections, optimizer updates, and FOAM-Mini variant are retained. Equation (4) corrects time indices to agree with the existing Algorithm 1; this does not establish a different optimization procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use C4 pre-training and GLUE/MMLU fine-tuning with the same task coverage. Long-context, prolonged-training, and quantized-state scenarios were already present in v1; no new dataset or test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LDAdamW as a comparator for LLaMA pre-training from 60M to 1.3B parameters. Other comparator sets are retained. SubTrack++ is added only to related work, while MUON/Muon and Full/Full-Adam are naming changes.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 replaces 2.5e-2 with 2.5e-3 in the reported learning-rate grid for GaLore, APOLLO, GWT, FOAM, and FOAM-Mini; Appendix B.1 also revises its grid. Table 2 changes its stated memory components to include gradients, although its retained values and Appendix B.2 accounting remain inconsistent with that description. These changes do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The fold-level, residual, scaling-factor, module-wise Adam, prolonged-training, long-context, quantization, and optimizer-integration analyses are retained, including the appendix plots. Figure 11 newly identifies its model as LLaMA-3B but presents the same residual ablation and curves.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly specifies three independent runs for the 60M–350M models, whose uncertainty values were already reported in v1. It removes the explicit statement that LLaMA-1.3B was not tested multiple times, without establishing additional runs there. The data-shuffling seed remains 42.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds LDAdamW perplexity and memory entries at four existing scales, with perplexities 29.27, 22.86, 17.53, and 14.88. Table 6 changes Full-Adam's Qwen-130M perplexity from 22.43 to 22.82. FOAM's numerical results and the retained experimental curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.3 changes from bounded stochastic gradients to bounded true gradients. Theorem 4.4 replaces the O(sigma^2) noise floor with O(sigma^2 log T / sqrt(T)) and changes the residual contribution from delta_l to delta_l squared. Appendix A substantially revises Lemmas A.2–A.3 and the theorem proof, redefining the approximation error relative to the true gradient and introducing a noise decomposition.

C1.justification: The abstract drops the claim of approximately 50% lower total training memory, and the introduction changes that claim to an end-to-end reduction of up to 50%. The central contributions—state folding with residual correction, Adam-like convergence, optimizer compatibility, and up to 90% optimizer-state savings—remain.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 extends its interpretation of parity with module-wise Adam by asserting lower memory use and higher throughput. Section 5.2 newly explains the omission of FOAM-Mini from fine-tuning experiments by the chosen fold level. The substantive future-work limitations in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository link and LDAdamW learning rates in Table 9. It also supplies training-token counts in Table 8, batch size 32 for Table 14, and the LLaMA-3B model identity in Figure 11. These are added documentation; the PDFs do not establish changes to those existing experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds LDAdam and SubTrack++ to the optimizer-related-work discussion and references. The overall positioning against projection, parameter-freezing, and shared-state approaches remains. The changed GWT reference title retains the same arXiv identifier and represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The main section and appendix organization is retained. V2 makes localized wording and terminology edits, corrects the GaLore-1/8 correspondence to FOAM-3, adds Impact Statement and Acknowledgements sections, and updates the correspondence address and publication header.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 9 gain LDAdamW rows, and Table 8 gains a training-token row. Table 13's incorrect timing/throughput caption is corrected to memory consumption. Other captions and labels are refined, Figure 8 moves below its discussion, and figures and tables undergo limited layout changes without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The added comparator, run-count disclosure, code link, and caption corrections improve assessment and reproducibility. However, the stronger convergence bound relies on Lemma A.3 setting a preconditioned noise term's expectation to zero without establishing the required cancellation despite dependence on V_t. Table 2 also newly claims to include gradients while Appendix B.2 still calculates only parameter and optimizer-state memory. These issues affect central theoretical and memory claims, making the net quality change uncertain.
